result:
Both my test servers are stopped. The site is fully fixed, built, and verified. Here's the summary:

## What was broken

The SaaS pivoted from **InboxZap** (email cleanup) to **Lumina** (AI meeting assistant), and the pivot left the site badly broken for SEO:
- Homepage content was all-Lumina, but every page's `<title>`/description still said "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes"
- The blog fetched a `/api/posts` endpoint that didn't exist — it just showed "Loading posts…" forever, to users and crawlers alike
- No individual blog post pages existed at all, despite 12 old post URLs sitting in Google's index with real demand (one at 3,900 impressions) stuck at position 40–60 earning almost no clicks
- `/features` and `/pricing` were linked in nav and listed in the sitemap but had no actual pages (404s)
- `/faq` redirected to `/#faq`, an anchor that didn't exist anywhere

## What I changed

- **Fixed metadata** site-wide (`app/layout.tsx`, per-page titles/descriptions matching real content, canonical URLs)
- **Rebuilt the blog as server-rendered**: `app/blog/posts.ts` holds 10 full posts, each targeting the specific high-impression query clusters from the GSC data (bulk-delete, Gmail storage, unsubscribe, filters, Outlook cleanup, etc.), with per-post metadata and `BlogPosting` schema
- **Added `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`** with internal links between related posts
- **Consolidated the two weakest posts** (post-3, post-7 — lowest impressions, no clear query match) into stronger related posts via 301s instead of leaving thin overlapping content
- **Created `/features` and `/pricing`** pages so nav/sitemap promises aren't dead ends
- **Added a real FAQ section** on the homepage (with `FAQPage` schema) including "What happened to InboxZap?" — so the branded search traffic that already ranks well isn't lost to confusion
- **Fixed the sitemap** to include all blog posts dynamically
- Added `llms.txt` and `SoftwareApplication`/`Organization` JSON-LD for AI-search visibility

Verified with a full production build and a local server: all pages 200, redirects 308 to the right targets, titles render correctly with no duplication, and sitemap.xml lists every real URL.

One thing worth flagging: `package.json` pins `next@14.2.5`, which npm warns has a known security vulnerability. That's a security fix, not an SEO one, so I left it alone — let me know if you'd like me to upgrade it separately.
